body: Biodiversity includes variation among individuals, among species and among ecosystems. Different species rely on different features of their surroundings. A forest and a coral reef differ in habitat, structure and exchanges of matter and energy, even without counting individual organisms.

A species becomes extinct if its last living members die. A species can also disappear from part of its former range while surviving elsewhere. Human changes to land and oceans, direct exploitation, climate change, pollution and introduced organisms can reduce local or global biodiversity.

limitations: Many species are poorly observed. Estimates of threatened species and of losses depend on observation, definitions, date and the scope of the assessment.
